summary: Mailbox-and-small-box musical instruments / accessories with high $/oz resale. Strict ship-class focus: harmonicas, microphones, effects pedals, mouthpieces, music boxes, pickups, DJ cartridges, small drum machines/samplers, ukuleles. Explicitly EXCLUDES guitars, basses, saxophones, trumpets, drum kits, amplifiers, pianos, full-size violins/cellos — the body+case footprint kills the freight math at typical resale prices. Sweet spot: $30-300 used resale on items that fit in a poly mailer or small priority-mail box.
field_workflow: Harmonicas: photograph the comb (wood vs plastic) + the cover-plate engraving; vintage 'Hohner Marine Band' wooden combs trade premium
Microphones: serial number + included accessories (mic clip, foam windscreen, original case) — full kit adds 30%
Microphones: condition test — plug into any preamp, listen for handling noise / cap drift / connector wiggle
Effects pedals: power up at the listing time, verify LED + footswitch + knob detents work
Effects pedals: vintage = original box + manual + Velcro = +30%; reissues are commodity
Mouthpieces: tip opening size (e.g. 7*) + facing length stamped — these drive the buyer search
Pickups: ohm-meter test the windings (humbucker should read 7-16k, single-coil 5-9k) — open coils kill resale
Music boxes: photograph the cylinder + comb teeth count; missing teeth = 50%+ value drop
skip_list: Banjo / mandolin (debatable; case too bulky for most priority mail)

era_markers: Hohner stamping on cover plate + Marine Band logo
Wooden comb (vintage) vs ABS plastic (modern Special 20+)
Made in Germany stamp (Hohner) — premium over modern
Lee Oskar color-coded packaging by key (red = G, etc.)
Seydel stainless-steel reeds (premium over brass)

comp_ranges_usd.item: Vintage Hohner Marine Band 1896 wooden comb

brands.notes: Harmonicas are the highest-$/oz musical instrument — palm-sized, fits in a bubble mailer for $5 USPS First-Class. Hohner Marine Band (since 1896) is the genre-defining piece; vintage examples with original wooden comb command premium. Lee Oskar / Suzuki / Seydel are the alt-premium tier. Avoid kid's harmonicas + plastic novelty sets — $5 commodity tier.

era_markers: Model number on the body or grille (Shure under the cartridge ring)
Made in Mexico (modern Shure) vs Made in USA (vintage Shure pre-2000) — vintage premium
Tube vs FET designation (Neumann U47 = tube, FET 47 = FET, different price tiers)
Original case + capsule covers + windscreen — full kit adds 30%
Vintage RCA / Telefunken / Coles ribbons — museum-tier $1000+
brands.notes: Microphones are the resale gold of recording gear — all small (palm-to-fist sized), all valuable. Shure SM58 is the safest commodity flip ($60-100); vintage Neumann / RCA / Telefunken are the apex ($1000-5000+). Verify capsule integrity by listening through any preamp before paying — diaphragm rust kills value. Reverb pays better than eBay for $200+ pieces; eBay better below $200.

era_markers: Boss compact pedals: pink-label (1977-88) vs black-label (1988-2002) vs current — pink premium
MXR Script Logo (1973-78) = vintage premium tier; block-logo modern = standard
Ibanez TS-808 (1979-82, JRC4558D chip) = original holy grail; TS-9 (1982-85) is reissue tier
Electro-Harmonix Big Muff: Triangle (1969-70), Ram's Head (1971-73), V3 Op-Amp (1977-78) = each generation a different tone + price tier
Klon Centaur (1994-2008) = the apex collector pedal — gold non-horsie versions $4-10k

comp_ranges_usd.item: Vintage Big Muff Triangle / Ram's Head

brands.notes: Effects pedals are the highest-leverage musical resale: small (3×5 inch typical), high collector premium for vintage. Reverb is the dominant pedal marketplace — sellers there pay 12% fee but reach the actual pedal-collector audience. Vintage Boss black-label, MXR script-logo, and Big Muff variants are the three deepest collector markets. Klon Centaur is the apex unicorn ($5K-12K) — verify hand-painted horsie before paying.

era_markers: Otto Link Florida (pre-1959 USA) = vintage premium tier
Selmer Paris hand-stamped 'S' = vintage; modern molded = standard
Tip opening number stamped on mouthpiece (e.g. '7*' = mid-open)
Original ligature + cap included = +20%
Hard rubber vs metal — different markets, different price tiers
brands.notes: Mouthpieces are pro-musician territory: small + high-margin. Otto Link Florida (pre-1959) is the saxophone-mouthpiece holy grail — even chipped examples trade $400+. Tip opening + facing length are critical search terms. Vandoren is the clarinet-mouthpiece volume play.

era_markers: Seymour Duncan model code (SH-1 = '59 humbucker, SH-4 = JB) on the cardboard sleeve / sticker
Pickup color (zebra / cream / black) — buyers search by color
Lead wire length original vs cut — uncut leads add 10-20%
Original mounting screws + springs + box add 10%
brands.notes: Standalone pickups (loose, not in a guitar) are perfect resale: poly-mailer ship + collector demand. Seymour Duncan + DiMarzio dominate the volume tier. Lollar / TV Jones / Fralin are the boutique tier with 2-3x markup. Verify resistance with multimeter before paying premium ($10 multimeter on Amazon).

era_markers: Reuge stamp on movement bedplate (Switzerland)
Cylinder pin count (more pins = longer / more complex tune)
Number of teeth on the comb (visible cant + missing teeth = damage)
Original key wind vs modern battery — keywind vintage premium
Polyphon / Regina / Stella disc-changer machines — apex-tier antique
brands.notes: Vintage music boxes are estate-auction sleepers — Reuge / Thorens / Lador / Sankyo are the Swiss premium tier. Verify the comb teeth are intact (point a phone flashlight under the comb — visible chips kill resale 50%+). Antique disc-changer machines (Polyphon / Regina / Stella) are museum-tier ($1500-8000) but rarely show at general estate sales.

era_markers: Roland TR-606 / 707 (1980s vintage) = collector tier
Korg Volca line: small footprint, $80-180 each, deep volume market
Teenage Engineering OP-1 (orange device) = the boutique apex
Boss DR drum machines: 1990s-2000s LCD models still trade $80-200
Original PSU + manual + box adds 15-20%
brands.notes: Compact drum machines / samplers: smaller than a textbook, ship in priority small box. Avoid bigger Roland MV / SP grooveboxes — those need medium box. Teenage Engineering OP-1 is the apex collector ($800-1400 used) — verify hardware buttons all work + screen pristine before paying.

era_markers: Shure M44-7 vs M44G — different stylus profile, different price tiers
Ortofon Concorde shape: integrated headshell + cart in one piece (unique)
Original needle/stylus tip cover included
Box + manual + screws/wires adds 20%

comp_ranges_usd.item: Shure M44-7 NOS new old stock

brands.notes: DJ cartridges are tiny ($50-400 each, fit in a padded envelope) — perfect $/oz resale. Shure discontinued the M44-7 line in 2018; NOS (new old stock) examples now command 2-3x original retail. Verify the stylus tip is intact (no diamond chip) under magnification before paying.

era_markers: Kamaka stamping on the headstock + Hawaii origin
Vintage Martin (pre-1965) = museum-tier; modern Martin still premium
Solid koa wood (Hawaiian premium) vs laminated
Soprano (smallest) / Concert / Tenor / Baritone — soprano + concert ship in small box
brands.notes: ONLY soprano / concert ukuleles for poly-mailer or small-box ship — tenor and baritone need medium box and price math gets thinner. Hawaiian-made (Kamaka, KoAloha, Kanile'a) are the resale gold — koa wood + family-shop construction. Vintage Martin Style 0 (1920s-50s) is museum-tier. Verify no top-cracks (stress lines from string tension) — top crack kills 70%+ of value.

platform_notes.Reverb: DOMINANT marketplace for musical instruments — pro musicians + collectors live here. Sellers pay 12% but reach the actual audience. Use for any item $100+. Shipping calculator built-in.
platform_notes.eBay: Better than Reverb on items <$100 (Reverb fee structure penalizes cheap flips). Use sold-listings filter; auction-style listings work for harmonicas / pickups / cartridges where the audience knows what they want.
platform_notes.Sweetwater: Reference for new-retail comp pricing; not a seller-friendly marketplace.
platform_notes.vintageguitarpedals.com / pedalgenie: Reference DBs for vintage Boss / MXR / Big Muff variants when authenticating.
